title: Dialect film screenings and the film "Dear You"
asked: MPs asked whether IMDA will review or abolish guidelines that restrict Chinese dialect films, allow general release in original dialect with subtitles, consider heritage value, and explain the factors behind the "Dear You" decision.
asked_by: Ms Valerie Lee, Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song, Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat, Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong, Mr Cai Yinzhou, Dr Neo Kok Beng, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Saktiandi Supaat
answered_by: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) and The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
response: Mr Tan Kiat How said IMDA's guidelines support promoting Mandarin as an official language, but IMDA has allowed flexibility: around 30 to 40 dialect films screen at festivals yearly, films like "881" have unrestricted screenings, and "Dear You" has 272 approved Teochew screenings with more possible if the distributor requests. He said there is scope to expand space for dialects while upholding Mandarin, with no dialect restrictions for arts or online content, Mandarin as the mainstay on free-to-air TV and radio, and more cinema screenings possible. He said IMDA is reviewing the film classification framework on dialect use and works with NHB on heritage context. Mr David Neo said MCCY supports Chinese dialect art forms through NAC funding, scholarships, the Chinese Opera Festival, and SG Culture Pass.

key_points.point: Around 30 to 40 dialect films are screened at film festivals each year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Each year, around 30 to 40 dialect films are screened at film festivals.

key_points.point: IMDA has allowed unrestricted screenings for films with substantial dialect use, including "881", "Long Long Time Ago" and "Wonderland".
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: IMDA has allowed unrestricted screenings of films with substantial use of dialect, such as "881", "Long Long Time Ago" and "Wonderland".

key_points.point: For "Dear You", IMDA approved 272 Teochew-version screenings and is prepared to approve more if the distributor requests them.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: For the film "Dear You", IMDA has approved a total of 272 screenings of the Teochew version and is prepared to approve additional screenings should the film distributor request them in response to audience demand.

key_points.point: There is scope to expand space for dialects while continuing to uphold Mandarin.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: There is, therefore, scope to consider how we can expand the space for dialects, while continuing to uphold the importance of Mandarin.

key_points.point: There are no dialect restrictions for arts performances or content on the Internet and online streaming services.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: For example, there are no dialect restrictions for arts performances or content available on the Internet and online streaming services.

key_points.point: On free-to-air television and radio, Mandarin should continue to be the mainstay.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: On free-to-air television and radio, we believe that Mandarin should continue to be the mainstay.

key_points.point: For cinemas, IMDA is prepared to allow more screenings of dialect-language films.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: For cinemas, we are prepared to allow more screenings of dialect-language films, so as to provide audiences with greater access to such content.

key_points.point: IMDA is reviewing the film classification framework on dialect use in films.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we are reviewing our current film classification framework with respect to the use of dialect in films.

key_points.point: IMDA works closely with Government agencies including the National Heritage Board.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: IMDA works very closely with different Government agencies including the NHB.

key_points.point: IMDA considers the context in which dialect is used in a film, including whether it reflects the cultural context of the time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: We do consider the context in which the dialect is used in the film – whether it is appropriate, reflects the cultural context of the movie of that time.

key_points.point: NAC funds the Traditional Arts Centre (Singapore) to encourage younger people to engage with Chinese opera in different dialects.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: NAC funds the Traditional Arts Centre (Singapore), which encourages the younger generation to engage with Chinese opera in different dialects.

key_points.point: In 2025, NAC funded 10 productions spanning Hokkien, Teochew, Cantonese and Hainanese opera.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: In 2025 alone, NAC funded 10 productions, spanning Hokkien, Teochew, Cantonese and Hainanese opera.

key_points.point: NAC invests in the next generation of dialect art form practitioners through scholarships.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: NAC also invests in the next generation of dialect art form practitioners through scholarships.

key_points.point: NHB works with heritage practitioners and clan associations to research and document dialects and cultural heritage.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: the NHB works very closely with heritage practitioners, clan associations and all who are keen, and they fund them as well, to research and to document our dialects and cultural heritage.

key_points.point: MCCY will continue to expand space for Chinese dialect art forms and nurture the next generation of practitioners.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: We will continue to expand the space for our Chinese dialect art forms and nurture the next generation of practitioners.

left_open: Whether foreign language films face equivalent linguistic audio restrictions.
Whether the historical rationale for mandatory Mandarin dubbing remains relevant.
Whether the Speak Mandarin Campaign rationale still applies given dialect use at home below 12%.
Whether the film classification framework includes an assessment of Intangible Cultural Heritage value.
Whether IMDA will publish clearer guidelines in advance for dialect general screenings.
Whether a radio station could be designated to play old songs with around 50% Mandarin and 50% dialects.
Whether the Government will review the relevance of the Chinese dialect policy in its current form.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on expanding dialect film screenings, heritage preservation, reviewing guidelines, and support for dialect arts and radio.
